title: On-prem Network Staging & SLA Migration Roadmap (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working draft for a staged rollout and SLA migration roadmap specific to on-prem VPC-style deployments (customer-managed networks / airgapped options). Goal: provide a repeatable pattern and Terraform module guidance so platform and SRE can onboard fleets of customer sites with predictable latency/availability SLOs and a clear rollback story.

Audience and scope:
- Primary: eng-private-deployments, platform SRE, solutions engineering.
- Scope: network staging, preflight validation, TF module knobs for cutover, SLA measurement probes, rollback gates, and post-cutover telemetry/ops runbook. Not covering app-level config (K8s manifests) except where network constraints require changes.

High-level rollout lanes (staged):
1) lab-simulate -> small lab cluster in our colo that mirrors customer VLAN/BGP/egress patterns (validate TF modules, mtu, path MTU discovery, jumbo frame settings).
2) pilot-tenant -> single customer non-prod tenant with dedicated peering (BGP/Static) and limited egress (HTTP proxy).
3) soft-production -> two non-critical production tenants with full monitoring, canary traffic shaping, and circuit-level failover.
4) broad-production -> full fleet activation with SLA escalation path and dedicated SRE on-call window.

Preflight checklist (what to validate BEFORE we schedule a cutover window):
- Network topology diagram from customer (subnets, VLAN IDs, NAT egress points).
- BGP neighbor config & ASN confirmation + L3 MTU known.
- Egress proxy / TLS intercept? Confirm certificate pinning implications.
- KMS/HSM integration plan (if customer uses external key manager).
- Firewall ACLs: allow control-plane CIDR and telemetry endpoints.
- Time sync & NTP reachability for audit logs.
- DNS delegation: confirm internal zones and split-horizon impacts.
- Terraform state access: ensure state backend access (S3/GCS or remote operator) or documented manual apply process for airgapped sites.
- PKI: certificate issuance plan and rotation windows.

Terraform module guidance / constraints (notes for module authors):
- Modules must expose a minimal set of flags for staging lanes: "staging_mode" (lab|pilot|prod), "enable_canary_route", "egress_proxy_host", "mtu_override". Keep defaults conservative.
- Avoid implicit resource replacement during staging. Provide a "plan-preview" helper script (tfshow wrapper) that outputs the diff in human-readable form.
- Modules should support two state backends patterns: remote (recommended) and local (airgap manual apply). Add example scripts for state migrations.
- Make BGP peering idempotent: track configured neighbors in a terraform local file when remote state not available to avoid accidental duplicate sessions.
- Provide a way to surface the expected downtime window in seconds for every change (calculated from known resource types that cause connection restarts).

Cutover sequence (pilot -> soft-prod):
- T minus 72h: run automated preflight validations, open change request in customer ticketing, confirm maintenance window.
- T minus 24h: deploy TF in dry-run mode, export expected route table diffs, submit to customer network team for review.
- T minus 1h: apply control-plane changes (peering, security group updates) while monitoring BGP established counts.
- T + 10m: start staged traffic injection (10% of production traffic routed through new path) using canary load generator.
- T + 30m: if latency and error budgets are within thresholds, escalate to 50% traffic.
- T + 120m: if still green, promote to 100% and begin deprecating legacy routes per retention policy.

Rollback criteria and plan:
- Immediate rollback triggers: BGP flap > 3 notifications in 5m, 10% increase in 95th percentile p50->p95 latency for tokenization endpoints, or >1% error rate increase for control-plane calls.
- Rollback mechanics: revert TF apply using stored plan snapshot + re-enable previous peering via explicit apply. Have manual CLI runbook for airgapped sites where remote state cannot be undone automatically.
- Post-rollback: capture diffs, ticket the root cause, and schedule a hard-freeze until a postmortem is completed.

SLA measurement probes (what we measure and how):
- Probe types: TCP handshake latency (to inference gateway), HTTP gen latency (simple POST/complete), KV cache hit ratio probe, model warmup latency sample.
- Measurement cadence: 10s probes for TCP/HTTP synthetic, 60s for internal cache warmup checks.
- Alerting thresholds: warn at 15% of SLA slack, page at 5% slack breach or sustained 3m violation.

Observability and tracing hooks (ops must have before cutover):
- Ensure token-level request IDs are passed end-to-end with route-tags so we can attribute latency to network vs runtime.
- Expose per-route metrics (egress path, peering id, AZ) in the console.
- Enable pcap-forensics toggle (disabled by default) that can be turned on for a 30-minute window in pilot for deep packet analysis.

Security and compliance notes (customer-facing considerations):
- HSM/KMS: validate remote KMS proxy or HSM crossconnect latency; document how key rotation will be coordinated and what window we need for contract adjustments.
- Data residency: map which control plane logs are stored externally and provide config knobs to zero-retain or forward to customer-owned logging.
- Audit: include a template audit checklist for SOC2 customers covering ingress/egress rules, cert rotation proof, and terraform plan archives.

Operational runbook snippets (to copy into pager doc):
- Quick verification commands:
  - check BGP status: "bgpctl show peers" (example output expected)
  - route table diff: "tfshow plan-diff --routes"
  - canary traffic generator: "canary-run --target <endpoint> --pct 10 --duration 10m"

Open questions / risks (to resolve before first pilot):
- How do we reduce blast radius if customer has asymmetric routing and we can only control one side of egress? (Options: source NAT at our edge, ephemeral reverse proxies).
- For airgapped installs where we cannot push TF, what's the approved customer-runbook that maps 1:1 to our module changes? Need sample playbooks.
- State drift detection in local-state workflows: explore a light-weight agent that periodically snapshots config and posts hashes to a secure collector.

Action items (short-term):
- [ ] Marco: produce tfshow wrapper and example output (ETA 2025-07-09).
- [ ] Jun: lab-simulate topology with jumbo frame variation and report stability (ETA 2025-07-11).
- [ ] Lydia: draft customer-facing preflight questionnaire and maintenance window template (ETA 2025-07-08).
- [ ] Aisha: coordinate pilot tenant schedule + open PD-1248 ticket.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the staging defaults very conservative; easier to escalate than to dial back after a replace.
- Watch out for module names that cause accidental resource replacement during state import. Add ID-migration notes.

References/links (handy):
- Confluence sketch: PD-ONPREM-STAGING-2025
- Terraform module repo PR: repo/terraform-modules#pr-342
- Canary tool: github.com/repo/canary-runner (internal fork)

If this looks reasonable for the team, I'll convert selected sections into a short pilot playbook (one-pager) that solutions engineering can hand to a customer's network ops team during kickoff.

-- Aisha
